name: ScrollStack
description: Cards stacked with their headers visible, driven by the page's scroll: a pile that forms as you scroll past it, or a formed stack that shuffles its front card to the back as you scroll. Pure CSS in both modes — no JavaScript at all.
whenToUse: Designs where stacked cards are DRIVEN BY SCROLLING rather than by clicks or swipes. Two shapes, and they are different answers rather than a detail to infer: `mode='pile'` when cards pin under one another as the reader scrolls past, the stack FORMING as they go; `mode='shuffle'` when the stack is already formed — every header visible as a rim — and stays pinned while scrolling sends the front card to the back, one card per scroll segment (scrolling up shuffles backwards). Pass the authored cards as children so the design's own card markup is kept; each card needs whatever should stay visible inside its first `peek` px. This ships NO JavaScript, so a section using it needs no `@hydrate`; the shuffle uses CSS scroll-driven animations and falls back to the pile under prefers-reduced-motion or where they are unsupported, so every card stays reachable. NOT for a deck the reader drives by clicking or swiping (that is CardStack), not for a row of cards that all fit (that is a grid), and not for a horizontal gallery (that is Carousel). Do not add a clipping ancestor — an ancestor scroll container breaks both the sticky pinning and the scroll timeline. In shuffle mode cards are clipped to the pinned box, so keep a card's content under a screen tall.

implements.note: Set peek to the height of whatever the design keeps visible on a covered card, and inset to 0 for a flush pile. Nothing here needs @hydrate — stepped `position: sticky` is the whole mechanism.

perCard sets the scroll length per shuffle in viewport-heights (default 0.75). Still no @hydrate: the scrub is a CSS scroll-driven animation, degrading to the pile under prefers-reduced-motion or without support. Cards are clipped to the pinned box — keep card content under a screen tall.
